title: Farmer
description: Tilling land, sowing, reaping, and raising animals for a lord or for subsistence.

title: Laborer / Plowman / Reaper
description: Performing general labor on an estate.

title: Shepherd / Animal Herder
description: Tending to livestock.

title: Miller
description: Operating a mill to grind grain, a relatively well-off but sometimes 'contemptible' profession.

title: Logger
description: Felling trees and preparing wood.

title: Hunter / Fisherman
description: Providing food through hunting or fishing.

title: Blacksmith
description: Forging tools, weapons, and general ironwork.

title: Carpenter
description: Working with wood to build structures and tools.

title: Stonemason
description: Cutting and shaping stone for buildings, from basic structures to cathedrals.

title: Weaver / Tailor
description: Producing cloth and making garments.

title: Shoemaker / Cobbler
description: Making new shoes (cordwainer) or repairing old ones (cobbler).

title: Potter
description: Making ceramic goods and pottery.

title: Butcher
description: Slaughtering animals and selling meat.

title: Baker
description: Baking bread and other goods.

title: Tanner
description: Processing animal skins into leather (a very dirty and low-status job).

title: Fuller
description: Clean wool with urine.

title: Minstrel / Busker
description: Traveling entertainers who sing and perform for food or money. Their stories are usually memorized and passed down orally.

title: Gong Farmer
description: A notoriously dirty job involving the removal of human waste from privies.

title: Messenger / Runner
description: Delivering messages and packages face-to-face.

title: Stablehand / Dockworker
description: Performing manual labor in stables, warehouses, or on the docks.

title: Refuse Picker
description: Collecting waste products from streets which could be used in manufacturing.

title: Inn Keeper / Tavern Owner
description: While some record-keeping might be involved, many smaller businesses relied on simple tally systems or hired a clerk for complex tasks.

title: Linkboy
description: Young assistants who carry torches or lanterns at night to guide people through dark city streets.

title: Ale-Conner
description: Officials who test the quality of beer. While a specialized role, it relies on sensory testing rather than reading.

title: Apothecary
description: Early pharmacists who read medical recipes and catalogue various herbs and chemicals.

title: Monk / Nun
description: Work in scriptoria, copying religious texts, scientific works, and legal documents, preserving knowledge.

title: Clergy
description: Priests and high-ranking church officials, often educated in Latin and theology, managing church records and administration.

title: Lawyer
description: University-trained, dealing with property, crime, and business, a role with increasing secular importance.

title: Notary
description: Highly specialized legal professionals who drafted binding contracts for property and business.

title: Chancery Clerk / Scrivener
description: Lay professionals who write documents for hire, handling legal and commercial paperwork.

title: Tax Collector
description: Record payments and manage revenues.

title: Steward / Bailiff
description: Senior staff for nobles, managing estates, records, and accounts.

title: Reeve
description: Estate managers who oversee farming operations for lords. They need to maintain ledgers and verify taxes.

title: Diplomat / Herald
description: These court officials have to read proclamations, recognize complex heraldic insignias, and negotiate treaties with foreign powers.

title: Merchant
description: Long distance traders, keeping ledgers for transactions.

title: Banker / Money Lender
description: Handles finances and debts.

title: Town Crier
description: While their job is oral, they are often literate officials who read out written public announcements to the populace.
